identificationModule.briefTitle: A Study of Rusfertide in Adults With Polycythemia Vera (PV)
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Phase 3 Study of the Hepcidin Mimetic Rusfertide (PTG-300; TAK-121) in Patients With Polycythemia Vera

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
Polycythemia vera (PV) is a long-term condition in which the bone marrow makes too many red blood cells (RBCs). Bone marrow is the soft tissue inside the large bones where blood cells are made. When there are too many RBCs, called erythrocytosis, the blood can become thicker and move less easily through blood vessels and organs. This can raise the risk of blood clots (thrombosis) in veins or arteries. Sometimes, these clots can be life-threatening and may cause a stroke or heart attack. Treatment aims to keep the percentage of RBCs in the blood (hematocrit) in a safe range. For adults with PV, this means keeping the hematocrit below 45%. This helps lower the blood thickness and the risk of thrombosis. PV can also be linked to low iron levels (iron deficiency), because the body uses iron to make more RBCs. Many people with PV are treated with blood removal (phlebotomy) to lower RBC levels in the blood. This can worsen the iron deficiency, because each blood removal also takes iron out of the body.

Rusfertide is a medicine that lowers the amount of iron available in the blood. It works like hepcidin, a natural hormone that helps control iron levels in the body. By limiting iron available for RBC production, rusfertide may help keep hematocrit below 45% and may improve symptoms. It may also reduce, or even remove, the need for phlebotomy in people.

The main aim of this study is to check how well rusfertide works compared with placebo to lower the number of phlebotomies. A placebo looks like rusfertide but does not have any medicine in it.

Other aims are to learn how safe rusfertide is compared with placebo and to understand how well it works to reduce the need for phlebotomy and to keep hematocrit levels under control. The study also wants to learn how rusfertide moves through the body (pharmacokinetics) and how it affects the body (pharmacodynamics or PD).

This study has 4 parts that follow each other:

* In part 1a, participants will receive either rusfertide or placebo.
* In part 1b, all participants will receive rusfertide.
* In part 2, participants can continue to receive rusfertide if they benefit from treatment with rusfertide.
* Part 3 will include participants who finish Part 2 and still benefit from rusfertide.

During the study, participants will visit the study clinical several times at fixed timepoints.

armGroups.label: Part 1a: Randomized, Double-Blind Period: Placebo
armGroups.description: Participants received their ongoing therapy for polycythemia vera (PV) along with rusfertide-matching placebo, subcutaneous (SC) injection, once weekly, from baseline up to Week 32.

armGroups.label: Part 1a: Randomized, Double-Blind Period: Rusfertide
armGroups.description: Participants received their ongoing therapy for PV along with rusfertide once weekly, SC injection, from baseline up to Week 32. Rusfertide doses were titrated to maintain hematocrit less than (\<) 45 percent (%). The starting dose was 19 milligrams (mg). The doses that were administered to Part 1a participants were 9.5, 19, 28, 41, 54, 69 and 82 mg.

armGroups.label: Part 1b: Open-Label Treatment Period: Rusfertide
armGroups.description: Participants received rusfertide once weekly, SC injection, from Weeks 32 to 52. Rusfertide doses were titrated to maintain hematocrit \< 45%. Participants who received rusfertide in Part 1a continued at their current dose unless dose adjustment was required. Participants who received placebo in Part 1a started rusfertide at 19 mg. The doses that were administered to Part 1b participants were 9.5, 19, 28, 41, 54, 69 and 82 mg.

armGroups.label: Part 2: Long Term Extension Period: Rusfertide
armGroups.description: Participants received rusfertide once weekly, SC injection, from Weeks 52 to 156. Rusfertide doses were titrated to maintain hematocrit \< 45%. The doses that were administered to Part 2 participants were 9.5, 19, 28, 41, 54, 69, 82, 95 and 108 mg. For weekly doses greater than (\>) 90 mg, the dose of rusfertide was and will be divided into 2 doses administered 3 to 4 days apart.

armGroups.label: Part 3: Treatment Extension Period: Rusfertide
armGroups.description: Participants will receive rusfertide once weekly, SC injection, from Week 156 to the end of the study (approximately 5 years). Rusfertide doses will be titrated to maintain hematocrit \< 45%. The doses that will be administered to Part 3 participants are 9.5, 19, 28, 41, 54, 69, 82, 95 and 108 mg. For weekly doses \> 90 mg, the dose of rusfertide will be divided into 2 doses administered 3 to 4 days apart.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1a: Percentage of Participants Who Achieved Response
primaryOutcomes.description: Response was defined as absence of phlebotomy eligibility. Phlebotomy eligibility was defined as either: 1) A confirmed hematocrit (HCT) greater than or equal to (≥) 45% that was at least 3% higher than the baseline HCT, where confirmation was defined as 2 consecutive HCT assessments that were ≥ 45% and at least 3% higher than the baseline HCT, or 2) HCT ≥ 48%.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1a: Number of Phlebotomies
Part 1a: Percentage of Participants With All Hematocrit Values < 45%
Part 1a: Change From Baseline in the Patient Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Fatigue Short Form 8a Total T-score
secondaryOutcomes.description: The PROMIS Fatigue SF 8a T-score will be obtained via the item-response theory (IRT) response-pattern scoring approach using the PROMIS Scoring Service available at https://www.assessmentcenter.net/ac\_scoringservice. It is an National Institutes of Health (NIH)-developed fatigue survey of 8 items that asks the participant about fatigue experience and impact over the past 7 days. Each item will be scored on a 5-point Likert scale (1=never/not at all to 5=almost always/very much). Raw scores (range: 8-40) will be converted into standardized T scores (range: 34.1-80.9), with higher scores indicating greater fatigue severity. A negative change from baseline indicates an improvement.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1a: Change From Baseline in the Myelofibrosis Symptom Assessment Form (MFSAF) Version 4.0 Total Symptom Score-7 (TSS7) Items
secondaryOutcomes.description: The MFSAF version 4.0 (v4.0) TSS7 is a questionnaire developed by the Patient-Reported Outcome (PRO) Consortium's Myelofibrosis Working Group that focuses on the 7 core symptoms of myelofibrosis: fatigue, night sweats, pruritus, abdominal discomfort, pain under the ribs on the left side, early satiety, and bone pain. It includes 7 items on a 0 (absent) to 10 (worst imaginable) numeric rating scale. A higher score indicates worse symptoms. A negative change from baseline indicates an improvement.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1a: Change From Baseline in the PROMIS Fatigue Short Form 8a Total T-score Among Participants Who Have Moderate or Severe Symptoms at Baseline
secondaryOutcomes.description: The PROMIS Fatigue SF 8a T-score will be obtained via the IRT response-pattern scoring approach using the PROMIS Scoring Service available at https://www.assessmentcenter.net/ac\_scoringservice. It is a National Institutes of Health (NIH)-developed fatigue survey of 8 items that asks the participant about fatigue experience and impact over the past 7 days. Each item will be scored on a 5-point Likert scale (1=never/not at all to 5=almost always/very much). Raw scores (range: 8-40) will be converted into standardized T scores (range: 34.1-80.9), with higher scores indicating greater fatigue severity. Moderate or severe symptoms are defined as a baseline PROMIS Fatigue SF 8aT-score \>/= 58.8. A negative change from baseline indicates an improvement.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1a: Change From Baseline in the MFSAF Total Symptom Score-4 Items (TSS4) Among Participants Who Have Moderate or Severe Symptoms at Baseline
secondaryOutcomes.description: The MFSAF v4.0 is a questionnaire developed by the PRO Consortium's Myelofibrosis Working Group that focused on the 7 core symptoms of myelofibrosis: fatigue, night sweats, pruritus, abdominal discomfort, pain under the ribs on the left side, early satiety, and bone pain. Items are scored on a 0 (absent) to 10 (worst imaginable) numeric rating scale. The MFSAF TSS4 is the sum of four items in the MFSAF (fatigue, itching \[pruritis\], night sweats, and abdominal discomfort). The weekly TSS4 will be calculated by averaging daily scores over a 7-day interval leading to Week 32 (inclusive). Moderate or severe symptoms are defined as a baseline MFSAF TSS4 \>/=9.1. A higher score indicates worse symptoms. A negative change from baseline indicates an improvement.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1a: Change From Baseline in the Myeloproliferative Neoplasm Symptom Assessment Form (MPN-SAF) Problems With Concentration Among Participants Who Have Moderate or Severe Symptoms at Baseline
secondaryOutcomes.description: MPN-SAF is a 10-item questionnaire measurement tool for symptoms of MPNs. Moderate or severe symptoms are defined as baseline MPN-SAF problems with concentration ≥4. The descriptive analysis approach the distribution of the MPN-SAF problems with concentration at Baseline will be categorized using the Patient Global Impression of Severity (PGI-S). The response quartiles will be used to establish the recommended cut-off points for the MPN-SAF Problems with Concentration corresponding to "none" or "mild" versus "moderate or "severe" categories on the PGI-S.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change From Baseline in the Individual Domain Scores and the Total European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30) Score
secondaryOutcomes.description: The EORTC QLQ-C30 is a validated instrument to obtain a participant's overall assessment of the impact of treatment on the participant's quality of life. It consists of 5 functional scales (physical, role, cognitive, emotional, and social functioning), a global quality of life (QoL) scale, 3 symptom scales (fatigue, nausea and vomiting, and pain), and 6 single items (appetite loss, diarrhea, dyspnea, constipation, insomnia, financial impact). For the functional and the global QoL scales, a higher score indicates better health. For the symptom scales, a higher score indicates more symptom burden. The QLQ-C30 summary score is calculated as the mean of the combined 13 QLQ-C30 scale and item scores (excluding global QoL and financial impact), with a higher score indicating a better health related QoL. Raw scores are converted into scale scores ranging from 0 to 100.

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion criteria:

1. Male and female participants aged 18 (or the minimum country specific age of consent if greater than \[\>\]18) years or older.
2. Participant understands the study procedures, is willing and able to adhere to study requirements and agrees to participate in the study by giving written informed consent.
3. Meet revised 2016 World Health Organization (WHO) criteria for the diagnosis of PV.
4. Phlebotomy requiring defined as ALL of the following:

   1. At least 3 phlebotomies due to inadequate hematocrit control in 28 weeks before randomization or at least 5 phlebotomies due to inadequate hematocrit control in 1 year before randomization, and
   2. Last phlebotomy due to inadequate hematocrit control within 3 months before randomization, and
   3. No phlebotomy within 6 days prior to randomization (do not include day of phlebotomy and day of randomization in the 6-day count).
5. Complete blood count (CBC) values immediately prior to randomization:

   1. Hematocrit \<45%,
   2. White blood cell count (WBC) 4000 cells per microlitre (/μL) to 20,000/μL (inclusive), and
   3. Platelets 100,000/μL to 1,000,000/μL (inclusive).
6. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0, 1 or 2.
7. Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) agree to use medically acceptable contraception (\<1% annual failure rate) during the study and for 30 days after the last dose of study drug.
8. A female participant must agree not to donate eggs (ova, oocytes) for the purposes of assisted reproduction during the study and for a period of 30 days after receiving the last dose of study medication.
9. Men with partners of childbearing potential agree to use medically acceptable contraception (\<1% annual failure rate) during the study and for 90 days after the last dose of study drug. In addition, men must use a condom during the study and for 90 days after the last dose of study drug regardless of the partner's childbearing potential.
10. A male participant must agree not to donate sperm for the purpose of reproduction during the study and for a minimum of 90 days after receiving the last dose.
11. Participants receiving cytoreductive therapy at randomization must be on a stable PV therapy regimen as follows:

    1. Hydroxyurea - at least 2 months
    2. Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor - at least 2 months
    3. Interferon - at least 6 months.
12. Participants treated with phlebotomy alone at randomization must have stopped:

    1. Hydroxyurea at least 2 months before screening
    2. JAK inhibitor at least 2 months before screening
    3. Interferon at least 6 months before screening.

Exclusion criteria:

1. Clinically meaningful laboratory abnormalities at Screening, including but not limited to the following:

   1. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) \<15 milliliters per minute per 1.73 square meters (mL/min/1.73 m\^2)
   2. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≥2.5×upper limit of normal (ULN)
   3. Total bilirubin \>1.5×ULN
2. Participants who required phlebotomy at HCT levels lower than 45%.
3. Pregnant or lactating females.
4. Clinically significant thrombosis (e.g., deep vein thrombosis or splenic vein thrombosis) within 2 months prior to randomization.
5. Active or chronic bleeding within 2 months prior to randomization.
6. Met the criteria for post-PV myelofibrosis as defined by the International Working Group-Myeloproliferative Neoplasms Research and Treatment.
7. Any infection requiring systemic therapy within 1 month of dosing except controlled human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B, and hepatitis C. Prophylactic therapies were allowed.
8. Any serious or unstable medical condition (e.g., poorly controlled HIV infection) or uncontrolled psychiatric condition as judged by the Investigator that would impair the participant's ability to participate in the study.
9. Major surgical procedure within 2 months prior to randomization unless the participant had fully recovered from surgery or planned major elective surgery during the study.
10. History of invasive malignancies within the last 5 years, except

    1. localized cured cancer (e.g., prostate cancer and cervical cancer)
    2. localized cured in situ or Stage 1 squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the skin, basal cell carcinoma (BCC) of the skin, or in situ melanoma of the skin.
11. Participants with in situ or Stage 1 SCC of the skin, in situ or Stage 1 BCC of the skin, or in situ melanoma of the skin identified during the required dermatology examination at Screening unless the cancer was adequately treated (i.e., treatment that was expected to be curative, such as Mohs surgery) before randomization. Note: Suspicious lesions were to be biopsied and results made available before randomization.
12. Participants with active alcohol or drug addiction that would have interfered with their ability to comply with study requirements.
13. Participants who did not complete at least 4 days of MFSAF assessments within 1 week prior to randomization.
14. Receipt of an investigational agent within 2 months or 5 half-lives, whichever was longer, prior to randomization.
15. Received busulfan, pipobroman, or 32Phosphorus within 7 months prior to Screening.
16. Participants with hypersensitivity to rusfertide or to any of the excipients or placebo.
17. Participants with any lesion or mass detected by physical examination or imaging during screening that was suspicious for malignancy unless evaluated and assessed to be not malignant.

participantFlowModule.preAssignmentDetails: This ongoing Phase 3 trial is planned to assess the efficacy \& safety of rusfertide along with current therapy for polycythemia vera (PV). The study consists of the following Parts: Part 1a 32-week placebo-controlled phase, Part 1b 20-week open-label rusfertide treatment, Part 2 104-week rusfertide long-term extension and Part 3 continued rusfertide treatment. Part 2 is ongoing \& Part 3 has not started as of data cutoff date 21 February 2025. Hence, data for Part 3 is not included here.
participantFlowModule.recruitmentDetails: A total of 293 participants participated in this study across 102 sites starting on 11 April 2022. This study is ongoing. Included here are the primary results.

groups.title: Part 1a: Randomized, Double-Blind Period: Placebo
groups.description: Participants received their ongoing therapy for polycythemia vera (PV) along with rusfertide-matching placebo, subcutaneous (SC) injection, once weekly, from baseline up to Week 32.

groups.title: Part 1a: Randomized, Double-Blind Period: Rusfertide
groups.description: Participants received their ongoing therapy for PV along with rusfertide once weekly, SC injection from baseline up to Week 32. Rusfertide doses were titrated to maintain hematocrit less than (\<) 45 percent (%). The starting dose was 19 milligrams (mg). The doses that were administered to Part 1a participants were 9.5, 19, 28, 41, 54, 69 and 82 mg.

groups.title: Part 1b: Open-Label Treatment Period: Rusfertide
groups.description: Participants received rusfertide once weekly, SC injection, from Weeks 32 to 52. Rusfertide doses were titrated to maintain hematocrit \< 45%. Participants who received rusfertide in Part 1a continued at their current dose unless dose adjustment was required. Participants who received placebo in Part 1a started rusfertide at 19 mg. The doses that were administered to Part 1b participants were 9.5, 19, 28, 41, 54, 69 and 82 mg.

groups.title: Part 2: Long Term Extension Period: Rusfertide
groups.description: Participants received rusfertide once weekly, SC injection, from Weeks 52 to 156. Rusfertide doses were titrated to maintain hematocrit \< 45%. The doses that were administered to Part 2 participants were 9.5, 19, 28, 41, 54, 69, 82, 95 and 108 mg. For weekly doses greater than (\>) 90 mg, the dose of rusfertide was divided into 2 doses administered 3 to 4 days apart.

achievements.comment: One participant discontinued the study due to adverse event before the start of Part 1b.

Part 1a: Change From Baseline in the Patient Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Fatigue Short Form 8a Total T-score
outcomeMeasures.description: The PROMIS Fatigue SF 8a T-score will be obtained via the item-response theory (IRT) response-pattern scoring approach using the PROMIS Scoring Service available at https://www.assessmentcenter.net/ac\_scoringservice. It is an National Institutes of Health (NIH)-developed fatigue survey of 8 items that asks the participant about fatigue experience and impact over the past 7 days. Each item will be scored on a 5-point Likert scale (1=never/not at all to 5=almost always/very much). Raw scores (range: 8-40) will be converted into standardized T scores (range: 34.1-80.9), with higher scores indicating greater fatigue severity. A negative change from baseline indicates an improvement.

outcomeMeasures.title: Part 1a: Change From Baseline in the Myelofibrosis Symptom Assessment Form (MFSAF) Version 4.0 Total Symptom Score-7 (TSS7) Items
outcomeMeasures.description: The MFSAF version 4.0 (v4.0) TSS7 is a questionnaire developed by the Patient-Reported Outcome (PRO) Consortium's Myelofibrosis Working Group that focuses on the 7 core symptoms of myelofibrosis: fatigue, night sweats, pruritus, abdominal discomfort, pain under the ribs on the left side, early satiety, and bone pain. It includes 7 items on a 0 (absent) to 10 (worst imaginable) numeric rating scale. A higher score indicates worse symptoms. A negative change from baseline indicates an improvement.

outcomeMeasures.title: Part 1a: Change From Baseline in the PROMIS Fatigue Short Form 8a Total T-score Among Participants Who Have Moderate or Severe Symptoms at Baseline
outcomeMeasures.description: The PROMIS Fatigue SF 8a T-score will be obtained via the IRT response-pattern scoring approach using the PROMIS Scoring Service available at https://www.assessmentcenter.net/ac\_scoringservice. It is a National Institutes of Health (NIH)-developed fatigue survey of 8 items that asks the participant about fatigue experience and impact over the past 7 days. Each item will be scored on a 5-point Likert scale (1=never/not at all to 5=almost always/very much). Raw scores (range: 8-40) will be converted into standardized T scores (range: 34.1-80.9), with higher scores indicating greater fatigue severity. Moderate or severe symptoms are defined as a baseline PROMIS Fatigue SF 8aT-score \>/= 58.8. A negative change from baseline indicates an improvement.

outcomeMeasures.title: Part 1a: Change From Baseline in the MFSAF Total Symptom Score-4 Items (TSS4) Among Participants Who Have Moderate or Severe Symptoms at Baseline
outcomeMeasures.description: The MFSAF v4.0 is a questionnaire developed by the PRO Consortium's Myelofibrosis Working Group that focused on the 7 core symptoms of myelofibrosis: fatigue, night sweats, pruritus, abdominal discomfort, pain under the ribs on the left side, early satiety, and bone pain. Items are scored on a 0 (absent) to 10 (worst imaginable) numeric rating scale. The MFSAF TSS4 is the sum of four items in the MFSAF (fatigue, itching \[pruritis\], night sweats, and abdominal discomfort). The weekly TSS4 will be calculated by averaging daily scores over a 7-day interval leading to Week 32 (inclusive). Moderate or severe symptoms are defined as a baseline MFSAF TSS4 \>/=9.1. A higher score indicates worse symptoms. A negative change from baseline indicates an improvement.

outcomeMeasures.title: Part 1a: Change From Baseline in the Myeloproliferative Neoplasm Symptom Assessment Form (MPN-SAF) Problems With Concentration Among Participants Who Have Moderate or Severe Symptoms at Baseline
outcomeMeasures.description: MPN-SAF is a 10-item questionnaire measurement tool for symptoms of MPNs. Moderate or severe symptoms are defined as baseline MPN-SAF problems with concentration ≥4. The descriptive analysis approach the distribution of the MPN-SAF problems with concentration at Baseline will be categorized using the Patient Global Impression of Severity (PGI-S). The response quartiles will be used to establish the recommended cut-off points for the MPN-SAF Problems with Concentration corresponding to "none" or "mild" versus "moderate or "severe" categories on the PGI-S.

outcomeMeasures.title: Change From Baseline in the Individual Domain Scores and the Total European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30) Score
outcomeMeasures.description: The EORTC QLQ-C30 is a validated instrument to obtain a participant's overall assessment of the impact of treatment on the participant's quality of life. It consists of 5 functional scales (physical, role, cognitive, emotional, and social functioning), a global quality of life (QoL) scale, 3 symptom scales (fatigue, nausea and vomiting, and pain), and 6 single items (appetite loss, diarrhea, dyspnea, constipation, insomnia, financial impact). For the functional and the global QoL scales, a higher score indicates better health. For the symptom scales, a higher score indicates more symptom burden. The QLQ-C30 summary score is calculated as the mean of the combined 13 QLQ-C30 scale and item scores (excluding global QoL and financial impact), with a higher score indicating a better health related QoL. Raw scores are converted into scale scores ranging from 0 to 100.
